about: Run, in order, by the desktop's real trashRepo.ts (apps/web/scripts/ios-conformance-fixtures.test.ts) and by the Swift core (TrashConformanceTests.swift) against the same starting database, which the TypeScript builds with the real repos. After every step both record the result and every row of notes, groups, trashed_notes, trashed_groups and sqlite_sequence; the two must match. The start: notebooks 1 (Notebook) and 2 (Work); groups 1 Projects (nb 2), 2 Sub (in 1), 3 Loose, 4 Empty, 5 Old group, 6 Edge group; notes 1 Alpha, 2 Beta (in 1), 3 Gamma (in 2), 4 Delta (in 3), 5 Epsilon, 6 Work note (nb 2), 7 Old, 8 Edge, 9 Recent, 10 Tie A, 11 Tie B. 'at' is when a trash step happens (the TypeScript sets the clock; Swift passes it); 'now' is purgeExpired's clock. A uuid not in the start database is compared as 'new'.

steps.note: a note goes to the Trash Can and comes back whole
a group with a note, or a sub-group, is refused and nothing changes
empty a branch, trash it, and restore from the bottom: the group is gone, so the note comes back at the top
the note's id has been taken: it comes back under a new id, with its uuid

steps.sql: INSERT INTO notes (id, title, created_at, updated_at, notebook_id) VALUES (4, 'Squatter', 'x', 'x', 1)

steps.note: another live note holds the uuid: it comes back with a new one

steps.sql: INSERT INTO notes (title, uuid, created_at, updated_at, notebook_id) SELECT 'Holder', uuid, 'x', 'x', 1 FROM trashed_notes WHERE id = 5

steps.note: a trashed row from an older build has no uuid
steps.sql: INSERT INTO trashed_notes (id, uuid, title, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, notebook_id) VALUES (77, NULL, 'Old build', 'x', 'x', '2026-02-03T00:00:00.000Z', 1)

steps.note: the notebook it was trashed from is gone: it goes to the first one
the retention window: one millisecond over 60 days is purged, exactly 60 days is kept
the list is most recent first, and the higher id first when two were deleted at once
